transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up an appointment someone else might need more, but... well, my wife actually suggested I come talk to you. 

It's probably just a small thing, but I guess I've been having a little trouble... catching everything she says. Like, she’ll be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or sorting out his rides, and I’m looking right at her, trying my very best to listen. But then a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. I feel awful about it because I really do care, and I don't want her to think I'm ignoring her. 

Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up here?
Have you noticed this trouble focusing and remembering conversations your whole life, or is this something new that started more recently?

Well, um, I suppose it's not exactly a new thing. I really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses for myself, but... even way back in grade school, definitely before I was twelve, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a bright kid. They were always very nice about it. But they did say I was always daydreaming a bit. 

I would accidentally leave my homework in my desk, or they'd have to give me little reminders to finish up my classwork. I was a good student, I promise, I wasn't trying to be rebellious or anything! I just... drifted off sometimes, I guess. 

I hope that answers your question? Is that the kind of background information you need?
Aside from these memory and focus issues, have you been feeling unusually worried, tense, or on edge lately, even about everyday things?

Oh, no, not really. I mean, I hope it's okay to say, but I actually feel pretty calm, for the most part. I don't want to sound like I'm not taking life seriously, but I really don't feel on edge or unusually worried about everyday things. 

My wife handles so much for us, bless her, and since I'm not working these days, I really don't have a lot of reasons to be tense. I just have that little bit of trouble with my focus, like I mentioned. 

Is... is that alright? I mean, am I answering that right, or did you mean a different kind of worry?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy over the past couple of weeks?

No, I haven't been feeling down or sad at all. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm depressed or unhappy. I actually have a very nice life, and I still really enjoy my hobbies. I like to tinker in the garage and read, and I still look forward to doing those things just as much as I always have. 

I'm generally a pretty cheerful person, I think. I just... well, I just get a little scattered sometimes, but it doesn't make me sad. 

I hope it's helpful to know that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are.

Besides trouble following conversations, do you currently have ongoing difficulties like losing your keys or belongings, forgetting appointments, or struggling to finish tasks you start around the house?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I struggle, exactly. I mean, I do misplace things now and then, but doesn't everyone at my age? I hope it doesn't make me sound careless, but I do seem to have a little habit of setting things down and forgetting where they went. 

Like my keys, or my phone, or... oh, sometimes the garden clippers if I'm out in the yard, or even old catering receipts I meant to file away. I'll just set them down for a second, and then I end up spending, oh, maybe ten minutes or so just retracing my steps to find them again. 

I always find them, though! I'm really not trying to be disorganized, it's just a little quirk, I suppose. I hope that doesn't sound too bad? I just want to be honest with you about it.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still for long periods, or find yourself talking more than others think is necessary?

Oh, no, not really. I mean, I hope I'm not giving the wrong impression, but I don't think I'm a restless person. I'm actually quite happy just sitting in my recliner reading a book or watching a little television. 

I don't think I talk too much either... at least, I hope I don't! My wife has never mentioned it, and I always try to be polite and listen when others are speaking. I certainly don't want to be a bother to anyone or take up too much space in a conversation. 

I mean, I might tap my foot sometimes if a good song comes on the radio, but I don't have any trouble sitting still. Does that sound normal to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have these attention and organization difficulties also caused problems for you in other areas of your life, like previous jobs, managing finances, or social situations outside the home?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a bad husband or anything, because I try my best, I really do. But, I suppose... well, my wife has been a little frustrated with me lately. 

We help take care of my cousin, you see, and I think she feels like she can't always count on me to remember the little details for that. I hate that it causes tension between us, because I really want to be helpful. I just... things slip my mind, I guess. 

And, oh, with the catering I do—just small jobs, nothing too crazy—I've noticed I have to double-check things a lot more, or even redo a task here and there just to make sure I haven't mixed anything up. I always get it right in the end, though! I just have to put a little extra effort in so the clients are happy. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything. I just want to be honest that it's, well, a little bumpy sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
